cards.title: Einstein’s relativity keeps your phone's GPS from getting lost
cards.body: Atomic clocks aboard GPS satellites tick faster than clocks on Earth. Earth's weaker gravity at orbital altitudes makes satellite clocks gain about 45 microseconds daily, while their orbital motion slows them by 7 microseconds. The net gain of 38 microseconds per day sounds tiny, but without correcting for Einstein's theories of relativity, navigational calculations would drift by roughly 10 kilometers every single day, making satellite navigation practically useless.

sources.title: Real-World Relativity: The GPS Navigation System

cards.title: The Sun takes 230 million years to complete one orbit around the galaxy
cards.body: Earth orbits the Sun every year, but our entire solar system is also journeying around the center of the Milky Way. Traveling at a breakneck speed of roughly 828,000 kilometers per hour, the Sun takes around 230 million years to complete a single circuit, known as a cosmic or galactic year. The last time our planet was in this same galactic neighborhood, the very first dinosaurs were just beginning to walk the Earth.

sources.title: How fast is the Solar System moving around the Milky Way?

cards.title: Planet-swallowing dust storms can blanket the entirety of Mars for months
cards.body: While dust storms on Earth remain local, Mars occasionally unleashes apocalyptic storms that wrap around the entire planet. Sunlight heats airborne red dust, generating thermal winds that loft even more particles in a runaway global feedback loop. These colossal dust blankets can last for months, blocking out over 99 percent of sunlight at the surface—a phenomenon that famously starved NASA's solar-powered Opportunity rover of energy in 2018, ending its 14-year mission.

sources.title: Opportunity Hunkers Down During Dust Storm on Mars

cards.title: Venus creates a magnetic shield out of the solar wind itself
cards.body: Unlike Earth, Venus possesses no internal dynamo to generate its own global magnetic field. Yet when the supersonic solar wind slams into Venus's thick upper atmosphere, it compresses and drapes the Sun's interplanetary magnetic field around the planet. This interaction creates an "induced magnetosphere." ESA's Venus Express mission showed that this makeshift shield deflects harmful solar particles, though energetic winds still steadily strip away traces of water vapor into interplanetary space.

sources.title: Venus' magnetic field: unusual interaction with solar wind

cards.title: Jupiter’s poles are ringed by eerily stable geometric clusters of cyclones
cards.body: When NASA's Juno spacecraft peered closely at Jupiter's poles, it revealed bizarre, enduring geometric patterns of massive cyclones. Instead of merging into one chaotic storm, eight monster cyclones tightly encircle a single central vortex at the north pole, forming a stable octagon. At the south pole, five—and later six—cyclones arrange themselves into a pentagon. Each storm spans thousands of kilometers, persisting in their locked polygonal dance for years without colliding or breaking apart.

sources.title: NASA's Juno Navigates Around Cyclonic Constellation at Jupiter's South Pole

quizzes.question: Without relativity corrections, how far would GPS location calculations drift off each day?
options: About 10 kilometers
About 100 meters
About 500 kilometers
Less than 1 meter
quizzes.explanation: Satellite atomic clocks gain 38 microseconds daily due to relativity, which compounds into roughly 10 kilometers of navigational drift every day.

quizzes.question: What creatures were just emerging on Earth the last time our solar system was in this part of the galaxy?
options: Dinosaurs
Trilobites
Woolly mammoths
Single-celled bacteria
quizzes.explanation: A galactic year takes about 230 million years. One orbit ago, early dinosaurs were just beginning to appear in the Triassic period.

quizzes.question: What caused the end of NASA's Opportunity rover mission on Mars in 2018?
options: A global dust storm blocked out sunlight
A wheel failure trapped it in sand
Its antenna was destroyed by a meteorite
Extreme cold permanently froze its battery
quizzes.explanation: A massive planet-wide dust storm blotted out over 99% of sunlight, preventing the solar-powered Opportunity rover from recharging.

quizzes.question: How does Venus possess a magnetic shield despite having no internal magnetic field?
options: The solar wind interacts with its ionosphere to induce one
Its volcanic core produces electric currents
A companion asteroid generates a magnetic wake
Its cloud layer acts as a giant static battery
quizzes.explanation: The solar wind compresses against Venus's upper atmosphere and drapes interplanetary magnetic field lines around it, forming an induced magnetosphere.

quizzes.question: What geometric cyclone pattern did NASA's Juno spacecraft discover surrounding Jupiter's north pole?
options: An octagon of eight cyclones around a central storm
A triangle of three colliding tempests
A single mega-hurricane spanning the whole pole
A square formed by four equal vortices
quizzes.explanation: Juno discovered eight giant cyclones stably arranged in an octagon around a single central polar vortex at Jupiter's north pole.

guesses.prompt: Without accounting for Einstein's relativity, how many kilometers would GPS location calculations drift off each day?
guesses.explanation: Satellite clocks tick 38 microseconds faster per day than ground clocks, causing uncorrected GPS positions to drift by ~10 km daily.

guesses.prompt: How many millions of years does it take our solar system to complete a single orbit around the Milky Way?
guesses.explanation: Known as a galactic year, the Sun takes roughly 230 million years to travel around the center of our galaxy at 828,000 km/h.

misconceptions.claim: Einstein's theory of relativity is purely theoretical and has no impact on consumer technology.
misconceptions.explanation: Smartphone GPS navigation depends on precise general and special relativity corrections; without them, location accuracy would drift by 10 km every day.

misconceptions.claim: Venus is completely unshielded from solar winds because it lacks an internal magnetic field.
misconceptions.explanation: Venus creates an induced magnetosphere as the supersonic solar wind drapes magnetic field lines against its upper atmosphere.

misconceptions.claim: Adjacent storm vortices in a planetary atmosphere will always merge into a single large vortex over time.
misconceptions.explanation: At Jupiter's poles, clusters of giant cyclones remain trapped in stable geometric arrangements for years without merging.
